sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:1
items.html: Draw from above downward from the Emanator: For at the time of the departure of the light of Keter — which comes about from the ascent of Malchut to ZA, to phase three — then the coupling of the upper light is made upon the screen of phase three, and ten Sefirot of direct light and reflected light are drawn in the level of Hochma, as is known. And in this way couplings were made in all the degrees along the way of the ascent of the screen to its refinement, as written above (in the Inner Observation, Part 2, Sub Header, “And therefore” — see there the whole passage). And this is what the ARI writes: “that although they ascend and depart, they draw from above downward from the Emanator a phase of light called reflected light.” For every coupling by striking draws reflected light from the upper light, since that portion of the light which is rejected by Malchut is called reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:2
items.html: A record, in the secret of “Set me as a seal upon thy heart”: The record resembles a seal, for just as the seal, after it departs from a place to which it was once adhered, is found to leave there its entire form, not lacking even the least thing, so is the way of the upper light: if it expanded into some place, then although it returned and departed from there, it leaves there its entire form, not lacking even a small impression; and in the end it will return and be revealed in that very same measure as at first.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:3
items.html:
A record, so that from there illumination will be drawn to the lower ones: And this applies both to light and to vessel, both in general and in particular. For from the records that are included in the Tabur of the first expansion of Adam Kadmon, which ascended to its Peh [mouth], there were born and emerged the Rosh [head], Toch and Sof [end] of the second expansion of AK, which is called Partzuf AB of AK, as clarified above (Part 3, in the Table of Answers, Item 210, see there). And likewise in particular: for the record that remains in the vessel of Keter [crown] of the first expansion becomes a male in the vessel of Keter of the second expansion; and from the record that remains in the vessel of Hochma of the first expansion, a vessel of a male is made in the vessel of Hochma of the second expansion. And from their coupling the males emerged in the rest of the Sefirot, as the ARI wrote in Etz Chaim (in the Gate of Mati veLo Mati [reaching and not reaching], Chapters 3 and 4).
And likewise, from the records that remain from the four levels which emerged at the time of the first departure — those that are called sparks, or letters, as written below — from them the females of the second expansion are made. For from the sparks that fell from the level of phase three, which is ZA, into the vessel of Malchut, which is phase four, there was made an inclusion of Malchut in ZA; so that afterwards, in the second expansion, when the light of Malchut clothed in the vessel of ZA, it found there the vessel of Malchut that belongs to it. And likewise, by force of the sparks that fell from the reflected light of the level of phase two, which is Bina, it brought about an inclusion of ZA in the vessel of Bina; so that afterwards, in the second expansion, when the light of ZA came and clothed in the vessel of Bina, it found there its own vessel; and so on in this way, as written below (in the Inner Light, in the explanation of the words of the ARI in Chapter 3, Item 80). Thus all the phases in the lower Partzuf are drawn only from the records that the Partzuf above it left. And this is what the ARI writes: “for the upper lights are to the lower lights in the phase of a father to sons” — meaning that a lower Partzuf is drawn from an upper Partzuf as a son from a father; that is, that it cascades from the self of the lights in the Partzuf above it, and this by means of the records that remain in the vessels of the upper Partzuf from its lights, as written above. And this is what the ARI wrote: “for the upper ones leave in the first place a little illumination called a record, so that from there illumination will be drawn to the lower ones,” as clarified. And remember this in all places, for it is the key to the cascading of the degrees by way of cause and consequence, from the Rosh of the line until the end of Assiya.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:4
items.html:
One record in its place: And one should not object that above, in Item 7, it says that from the record the existence of the vessel is made, while here it says that there is already a vessel even before the record and before the departure of the light. The matter is that there are two kinds of vessels in every Partzuf, namely: vessels that are drawn from the first look in Malchut of the Rosh [head] — for that Malchut widens by the force of the reflected light in her which she raised from below upward, and she expands from herself within herself into ten Sefirot from above downward, and these are regarded as a vessel of reception for the first expansion. And there is a further phase of vessels in the Partzuf, drawn by means of the second look in Malchut of the Guf [body] of the Partzuf, which causes the departure and the return of that light to the Emanator; for the records that remain after that departure became complete vessels, as the ARI wrote (above, in Part 3, Chapter 12, in the Inner Light).
Now all these records of the second look draw to all the phases, to its lower Partzuf, as written (see above item). And this is what is said: “for the upper lights are to the lower lights in the phase of a father to sons” — meaning that the lower Partzuf is drawn from the upper Partzuf as a son from a father; that is, by means of the records that remain inside the vessels of the upper Partzuf from its lights, as above (see above item). And this is what the ARI writes: “for the upper ones leave in the first place a little illumination called a record, so that from there illumination will be drawn to the lower ones,” as clarified. And remember this very well, for it is the key to the cascading of the degrees by way of cause and consequence, from the Rosh of the line until the end of Assiya — that every lower one is a consequence brought about by the records of the Partzuf above it.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:5
items.html: Illumination is drawn to the light of Hochma: For afterwards, when Malchut ascended to phase three, where ten Sefirot emerge in the level of Hochma, it is impossible for this light to begin in the Sefira of Hochma, since every expansion of light must begin from Keter [crown]; and therefore she requires the illumination of the record of Keter, for through this the light is adhered and bound to the root. And likewise, when Malchut ascended to Bina and ten Sefirot emerge in the level of Bina, the illumination of the records of Keter and Hochma necessarily remains there, and so forth in this way, for the reason stated. And remember this in all places, for it is entirely impossible for any degree to be wholly lacking the upper Sefirot within it; rather, at the time when the upper Sefirot are in the phase of the illumination of a record alone, then we call them lacking there, since they are there without illuminating.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:6
items.html: Malchut, when she departs, does not leave a record in her vessel: For it is a female light, which receives for herself and does not bestow; and for this reason her ten Sefirot are found to conclude the degree, for it is the secret of reflected light alone, as is known. And therefore she does not leave a record, since a record is nothing but the remnants of the expansion of direct light that remain there, as in the words of the ARI above. And also there is no interruption here in the upper light, as above (see above item), for the lower one is dependent upon the upper one, but the upper one has no need of the lower one.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:7
items.html: She is not of their kind and she has no adhesion with them: Because they come in a renewed form of coarseness, therefore she has no adhesion with them; for adhesion means equivalence of form, while distinction and separation mean disparity of form, as is known. (See Part 3, answer 210.)

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:8
items.html:
This is another cause why Malchut is called poor, who has nothing of her own: The ARI has already written the reason why Malchut is called “that does not shine”: it is because in the second expansion the ten Sefirot were drawn only in the level of Hochma, and the light of Keter [crown] remained concealed in the Peh [mouth]. And therefore it comes about that the light of Hochma comes into the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina into the vessel of Hochma, and the light of ZA into the vessel of Bina, and the light of Malchut into the vessel of ZA — and thus the vessel of Malchut remained without light. And therefore she is called a mirror that does not shine. (See Etz Chaim, Gate 6, Chapter 5.) And here he adds a second reason as well, namely, for the reason that Malchut left no record after her in the first expansion.
And one should not object: if the light of Keter is concealed from the second expansion, the vessel of Keter should have remained there without light — so why were the lights interchanged, such that the light of Hochma comes into the vessel of Keter, until the vessel of Malchut remained without light? Indeed this has already been clarified in the Inner Observation (Part 2, Chapter 8): it is because the way of the lights is to clothe only in the more refined vessels that are found in the Partzuf; and even if there is nothing there but the light of Nefesh alone, she clothes only in the uppermost vessel, that is, in Keter, and the nine lower ones remain without light — see there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:9
items.html: Two kinds of light: For the first expansion, which is drawn by means of the widening of Malchut from herself within herself into ten Sefirot down to Malchut of the Guf [body] — which is drawn from above downward, that is, to the phase of clothing — is the one called direct light, mercy. And likewise all the records that remain from those ten Sefirot after this light has departed are also direct light, mercy, only in the phase of a scant illumination, which is called a record. Indeed those levels which emerge by means of a coupling by striking, along the way of the ascents of Malchut and her refinement from degree to degree from below upward until all the light is concealed — all these levels are called reflected light, judgement, since the levels go on diminishing until complete departure.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:10
items.html:
The coarse light joined with the refined light: That is to say, when the light expands from Malchut of the Rosh [head] downward to the Guf [body], this light is comprised of direct light and reflected light, that is, just as they clothe one another in the Rosh. Now the direct light is called by the name “the refined light,” and the reflected light is called by the name “the coarse light,” since it is drawn by the force of the coarseness and the restriction in the screen of Malchut of the Rosh. And although above, in the Rosh, there is no discernment of coarseness in it at all — since it ascends and clothes the first nine Sefirot which are from the screen upward, and the force of the coarseness cannot act above the place of its revelation and its existence, not even a little — indeed afterwards, when this reflected light expands and descends together with the direct light within it, from Malchut of the Rosh downward, it is certainly found that the coarseness in the screen already dwells in it; only that it is not regarded as a deficiency at all, for all its merit is bound up in the coarseness, since without her there would be no light whatsoever in the Partzuf. Yet in the end, after the light has departed from the Partzuf and the coarseness has been emptied of that direct light which was clothed in her, then that measure of coarseness was revealed in all its deficiency and all its lowliness as against the direct light.
And this is what the ARI writes: “and it remained below” — meaning, after the refined light has been emptied out of the coarse light, that is, after the direct light departed and was drawn out of the reflected light that had clothed it, the coarse light remained below; meaning that the inferiority of the reflected light as against the direct light was revealed. And this is what he says, that this coarse light, which remained below after the return of the refined light upward, “is the phase of the vessels themselves” — meaning that this reflected light, which was emptied of direct light after its first expansion, is the whole of the material in the vessels of this Partzuf, which is called the first expansion of AK, or Partzuf Galgalta of AK; and within it the record and the sparks of the descending reflected light were clothed. And it will be clarified before us that this record and these sparks of reflected light were made and corrected into vessels for the Partzuf after it, which is called the second expansion, or AB.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 4:2:11
items.html:
Coarse light, which is the phase of the vessels: That is, the reflected light that remains after the departure of the direct light from within it, as above (see above item). Indeed we must understand very well the matter of the ascent of the lights that has been stated, and know precisely what ascended and what was refined, and what remained below and became the phase of vessels.
And you already know the matter of the screen, whose meaning is “a force of restraint upon the upper light, that it should not expand inside the four phases of coarseness that are in phase four, which is called Malchut,” as written well (in Part 2, in the Inner Observation, Chapter 2).
And as for the matter of the ascent of Malchut to ZA in the words of the ARI below, know that it revolves upon the screen and the reflected light in her alone; and these two are called in the words of the ARI by the name “the light of Malchut,” and they are called by the name “light” because there is no other light in Malchut from the time of the restriction onward. But the vessel of Malchut herself cannot ascend to ZA, since an ascent means refinement, as is known, and this is possible only in the screen but not in the vessels, for this matter of refinement does not apply to the vessels at all. Rather, that measure of coarseness which is in the phase of the vessels in each and every Partzuf remains fixed and enduring so for ever, until they receive their correction. And this has already been clarified (in Part 2, answer 43, see there).
And the matter of the refinement of the screen from phase four to phase three means that, because of the clash of the inner light and the surrounding light in the screen, the last phase of the coarseness that was included in its force of restraint became concealed and was lost from it.
And it follows from now on that it restrains the upper light from expanding except to phase three of the coarseness that remains in it, for phase four within phase four is no longer included in it now. And it follows that it restrains and returns the upper light only from the three phases of coarseness that remained included in it out of phase four; and the reflected light returned from these three phases suffices to clothe the direct light only up to Hochma, and in its clothing it does not reach up to Keter [crown]. And thus it follows of itself that the light of Keter is concealed from the Partzuf, since no light is grasped in a Partzuf without a garment and a vessel, as written well in the Inner Observation (Part 2, Chapter 7, Sub Header, “And the reason”).
And it has been well clarified that the matter of the ascent and the refinement is an occurrence of the screen, and does not pertain to the vessels at all. And the matter of the vessels, which remained in their place after the departure of the direct light — that which is called in the words of the ARI “the coarse light” — these are the four phases of coarseness included in that reflected light which has already come to actual clothing, which clothed the ten Sefirot of the Guf that have now been emptied of their lights, as written above (see above item).
